result.note: Tests India's August 2026 WTO consultation request on the US quartz safeguard and why earlier US tariff disputes were treated differently.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India requested consultations at the WTO over a US safeguard measure on quartz surfaces. Consider the following statements:
items: The safeguard followed a finding by the US International Trade Commission that rising imports had seriously injured domestic manufacturers.
India has been exempted from the safeguard duties.
According to the Global Trade Research Initiative, the US bought 72.5 per cent of India's quartz-surface exports in the 2026 financial year.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the story states that India is not exempt. First-year imports face an additional 25 per cent tariff within the quota and 50 per cent above it, and India's quartz-surface exports to the US were worth USD 233.3 million in FY2026.
questions.source: The US International Trade Commission found rising imports had seriously injured domestic manufacturers.

questions.prompt: Before its August 2026 WTO request on quartz surfaces, India had sought consultations over US tariffs on steel, aluminium, automobiles and copper. On what ground did Washington reject those requests?
questions.explain: Washington treated those tariffs as national-security measures, not safeguards. Because the quartz measure is explicitly a safeguard, India has cleaner procedural ground at the WTO this time.
questions.source: Washington rejected them as national-security measures, not safeguards.
